newsitem.title: USA: CME live and feeder cattle expected higher.
newsitem.headline: CME live and feeder cattle expected higher.

text.p: CME live cattle futures were expected to open 0.100 to 0.200 cent per lb higher while feeder cattle futures were called 0.200 to 0.400 cent a lb higher, livestock analysts said.

Further advances in cash beef prices Monday and expected further strength in fed cattle markets were expected to lift live cattle futures. Expected lower corn futures should also lend support to deferreds, analysts said.
Boxed beef cut-out values rose $1.15 to $0.57 per cwt Monday with heavy-weight choice up to $107.38, the highest level since March 5.

However, expectations that cash prices may be near a top and could slip soon on seasonal pressure may weigh on June. Rolling of long June positions into August was also expected to continue and limit any gain in June, analysts said.

Fed cattle supplies are projected to expand soon, based on previous Cattle-on-Feed reports, and beef markets are seen topping soon as retailers complete purchases for Mothers Day and Memorial Day. Early indications on the next Cattle-on-Feed report also indicated heavy placements and large on-feed supplies, they added.

Renewed demand was seen in feeder cattle futures after values slipped late Monday. A large jump in the latest CME feeder cattle index and weaker corn futures indications based on active plantings should prompt demand in feeders early, they said.
The latest CME feeder cattle index jumped $1.21 to $73.34 per cwt, the highest level since February 16, 1995.
